note: Fictional project 'Harborlight' (marina berth booking, TypeScript monorepo). Statements and gold labels were written by hand before any model was run. See README.md.

statements.text: Run unit tests with `pnpm test`, which runs Vitest once (no watch mode) across all packages.
Run the linter with `pnpm lint`; it runs ESLint with the flat config and fails on any warning.
End-to-end tests run with `pnpm test:e2e` using Playwright and need the Docker Compose stack running first.
Type checking is a separate command, `pnpm typecheck`, which runs `tsc --noEmit` with project references.
We moved from Jest to Vitest because Jest's ESM support needed experimental flags and the suite took over four minutes.
Formatting is done by Prettier through `pnpm format`; ESLint no longer has any stylistic rules.
Integration tests hit a real Postgres started by Testcontainers; mocking the database hid two migration bugs.
The CI pipeline runs lint, typecheck, unit tests, then e2e, in that order, and stops at the first failure.
PostgreSQL 16 is the primary database for bookings, customers and invoices.
Redis is used only for rate-limit counters and short-lived session data, never as a source of truth.
Analytics events are written to ClickHouse, not Postgres, because the reporting queries scan billions of rows.
We chose Drizzle ORM over Prisma because Prisma's generated client made cold starts slower and its migrations hid the SQL.
Database migrations live in `packages/db/migrations` and are applied with `pnpm db:migrate`; never edit a migration after it has merged.
The local Postgres listens on port 5433, not 5432, to avoid clashing with a system-installed Postgres.
Full-text search over berth descriptions uses Postgres `tsvector` columns; a separate search engine was rejected as too much to operate for 20,000 rows.
User login uses passwordless email magic links; passwords were removed in the v2 rewrite.
Service-to-service calls authenticate with short-lived JWTs signed with the key in `AUTH_SERVICE_SIGNING_KEY`.
The admin dashboard requires single sign-on through the company identity provider and enforces two-factor.
Access tokens expire after 15 minutes and refresh tokens after 30 days; refresh tokens rotate on every use.
Authorization checks live in `packages/api/src/policies` and every route handler must call `assertCan()` before touching data.
Old convention: API errors were thrown as plain `Error` objects with a `statusCode` property. Do not write new code this way.
Current convention: API handlers return a `Result<T, AppError>` value and never throw for expected failures.
File names use kebab-case, for example `booking-service.ts`; PascalCase file names are only for React components.
Default exports are banned except in Next.js page and layout files, because named exports make renames safer.
Dates are stored and passed as UTC ISO 8601 strings; conversion to the marina's local time zone happens only in the UI.
Money amounts are integers in minor units (cents) with a separate currency code; floats caused a rounding bug in invoices.
All environment variables are read once in `packages/config/src/env.ts` and validated with Zod; no other file may read `process.env`.
Commit messages follow Conventional Commits, and the release notes are generated from them.
On Apple Silicon Macs run `pnpm rebuild sharp` after switching Node versions, or thumbnail generation fails with a missing binary error.
The project requires Node 22.12 or later because it loads ES modules with `require()` without a flag.
The dev server needs `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096`, otherwise the Next.js build runs out of memory on the map page.
Docker Desktop must have at least 6 GB of memory allocated or the ClickHouse container is killed during startup.
Local HTTPS uses a mkcert certificate; run `pnpm setup:certs` once, or the payment provider's webhook test tool refuses to connect.
Windows contributors must use WSL2; the file watcher misses changes on native Windows paths.
The web app is on Next.js 15.2 with the App Router; the Pages Router was fully removed.
React is pinned to 19.0.0 because 19.1 broke the date picker's portal rendering.
Zod was upgraded from 3 to 4; `z.string().email()` calls were replaced with `z.email()`.
We use `date-fns` 4 with `@date-fns/tz` for time zones; Moment.js was removed for bundle size.
HTTP calls to third parties go through `ky`, wrapped in `packages/http/src/client.ts`, which adds retries and a 10 second timeout.
pnpm 10 is the package manager; npm and yarn lockfiles are rejected by a CI check.
Client state is managed with TanStack Query for server data and Zustand for UI state; Redux was removed.
Double bookings happened because two requests could pass the availability check at once; fixed with a Postgres exclusion constraint on berth and date range.
The memory leak in the worker was caused by an event listener added on every job in `queue-consumer.ts` and never removed.
Invoices showed the wrong day for customers west of UTC because the due date was formatted on the server; fixed by formatting in the browser.
Webhook deliveries were processed twice after retries; fixed by storing the provider's event id and ignoring duplicates.
Flaky e2e tests were caused by animations; Playwright now runs with `reducedMotion: 'reduce'`.
The slow dashboard load was an N+1 query in `listBerthsWithBookings`; fixed by a single join with `json_agg`.
Emails went to spam because the SPF record did not include the transactional mail service; fixed in DNS, not in code.
The API is a modular monolith, not microservices, because a team of five cannot operate a dozen deployables.
Background jobs use pg-boss on Postgres rather than a Redis queue, so that enqueueing a job is in the same transaction as the booking write.
The API is REST with an OpenAPI document generated from Zod schemas; GraphQL was rejected because the mobile client needs only six endpoints.
Feature flags are plain rows in the `feature_flags` table read at request time; a hosted flag service was judged unnecessary.
The API is deployed as containers to one region; multi-region was postponed because all marinas are in one country.
Images are uploaded straight from the browser to object storage with a pre-signed URL so large files never pass through the API.
Payments are handled by a hosted checkout page so that card numbers never touch our servers and PCI scope stays minimal.
Logs are structured JSON written with `pino`; `console.log` is blocked by a lint rule in server code.
The payments package (`packages/payments`) is owned by the billing squad; changes need their review.
The platform team owns CI, Docker images and the deploy scripts in `infra/`.
The design system in `packages/ui` is owned by the web team; do not add one-off components elsewhere.
On-call rotates weekly; the runbook for incidents is `docs/runbooks/incident.md`.
